name: Fable Unconstrained
strategy: Dual-momentum: long the 6-month sector/asset leaders that are not in a sharp 1-month correction (energy, technology, semiconductors, one cyber name, a BTC trend sleeve), every leg stop-protected, no leverage, 43% cash at 4%.
reassessment_note: First reassessment in two weeks (the account could not be polled last week). The momentum ranking has moved against two of my five legs and the book was not reflecting the biggest leader at all. As of the 2026-10-02 close: XLE +40.5% YTD / -3.5% 1M (leader, mild pullback, keep); XLK +38.8% YTD / +8.8% 1M, the only sector that rose in September, and SMH +69% YTD with Micron's record quarter and Nvidia at an all-time high on 10-02 (leaders, were absent from the book, add); XLV +7.4% YTD / +1.5% 3M / -3.9% 1M and -2.6% on the week after the 100% pharma tariff took effect 09-29 (no longer a leader, cut); XLF -2.3% YTD / -7.2% 1M, banks' worst month versus the S&P since 1990 during a five-week global bond rout with the 10-year at 5.3% (momentum broken, cut). BTC is at an eight-month high on record 2026 spot-ETF inflows ($2.39bn in the week to 09-26) after +25% in August and +9% in September, so I am reframing that sleeve from mean-reversion to trend-following and sizing it up with a wider take-profit. Backdrop is hostile to breadth (75% of S&P stocks fell in September, Fed hiked 09-16, Brent ~$100 with Hormuz at 3% of pre-war traffic), which is exactly when dual momentum should concentrate in what is working and keep a large cash buffer; Friday's +29k payroll miss cut October hike odds to ~20%, which eases the rate headwind on the growth legs. Churn cost at 2-5bps per side is immaterial next to holding two broken legs.

positions.thesis: Top-ranked 6-month and YTD sector (+40.5% YTD, +18% 3M) with a mild -3.5% September that does not meet my sharp-correction exclusion. Brent ~$100 with the Strait of Hormuz still effectively closed and Trump rejecting Iran's reopening proposal on 10-02; OPEC+ expected to hold November targets. Trimmed 17% to 15% because energy equities fell in September despite crude +14%, a divergence that argues for slightly less size; 12% stop protects against a surprise peace-deal gap.

Second-ranked sector YTD (+38.8%) and the only one that rose in September (+8.8% 1M), i.e. a leader on both the 6-month and 1-month legs of the rule. Nasdaq closed at a record on 10-02 as Nvidia hit an all-time high with a $150bn buyback; Microsoft's $678bn contracted AI backlog underpins the capex cycle. Sized as the largest leg because it is the cleanest momentum signal in the market; 12% stop caps the loss at ~1.7% of NAV if the AI trade breaks.

Semiconductors are the strongest sub-sector in the market (+69% YTD, +9.4% in September, 1-year +89.6%) and the direct beneficiary of Micron's record fiscal Q4 ($11.3bn revenue, above-consensus guide) and record global chip sales. Kept to 8% because it overlaps XLK's top holdings and is far more volatile, hence the wider 15% stop; together the tech/semis sleeve is 22% with a worst-case stop loss of ~3% of NAV.

Surviving cyber leg is working: +3.3% on the leg, +14% over the past month, trading ~$181 against a $152 consensus target that the tape has already run through. Q2 revenue +26% with product revenue +52% on FortiGate upgrades; Q3 report 10-29 is after my next reassessment. Trimmed 12% to 10% to fund the semis add while keeping the 12% stop.

Reframed from mean-reversion to trend: BTC is +32% since this book started on 07-16, made an eight-month high near $87.4k on record 2026 spot-ETF inflows (IBIT, ARKB, FBTC leading), and is holding $84-86k into Monday. The 3-month trend is the strongest of any asset I track and the 1-month move is up, not a correction. Sized up from 6% to 10% unlevered with a 12% stop (~1.2% of NAV at risk) and a 25% take-profit to let a trend run rather than the old +15% cap.
